I decided to email them anyway, pretending I left a review, and asked for the free item. They responded positively, and today I received the gift, which was another one of the same item. Now, when I checked the seller's ratings, they have over 1000 reviews, all positive. That makes me think they've been doing this for a while. Inside today's package, there was another thank you note for my review (even though I haven't left one yet) and a reminder that for all their items, a 5-star review equals a free item. So, the question is, should I report them to Amazon after receiving the free item? If I do, what should I do instead? Amazon has strict guidelines against sellers offering incentives for reviews because it can lead to fake or biased reviews, which aren't fair to other customers. By offering free items, the seller is encouraging positive reviews, which might not be genuine. That seems wrong because it's manipulating the review system. From a Christian perspective, I should think about honesty and fairness. The Bible teaches us to be truthful and to do unto others as we would have them do unto us. Offering incentives for reviews isn't honest because it's trying to get people to say positive things they might not genuinely feel. It's also unfair to other sellers who play by the rules and to customers who rely on genuine reviews to make purchasing decisions. I also need to consider the consequences of reporting.
